::: {.why}
Nobody reads a forty-page report, and the two-page version is a different document rather than a shorter one, which is why it takes a day rather than an hour.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Produce two-page versions of three milestones, each readable in ten minutes by someone who has not seen the rest.
- Have each open with the result and the caveat rather than with the method.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Write the two-page version of the platform, the alpha book and the option pricer: what it is, one figure, the result with its interval, the specification count where relevant, and the limitation you consider most serious. Method goes in a short section rather than at the front.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Test them: give one to someone outside the field and ask what they think it claims. Where they get it wrong, the document is wrong rather than the reader. If nobody is available, leave it for a day and reread it cold, which catches perhaps half of what a reader would.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The three write-ups are the form in which the year's work actually gets read: result first, one figure, interval, specification count, and the most serious limitation, each in two pages.
:::
